skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray showing interstitial lung disease patterns to distinguish between fibrotic, cystic, and consolidative etiologies.
steps: Assess lung volumes to determine if restriction (low volumes) or hyperinflation is present.

Identify the dominant parenchymal pattern: reticular/net-like opacities suggest fibrosis; cysts/nodules suggest histiocytosis; patchy consolidation suggests organizing pneumonia; ground-glass suggests hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
Evaluate the distribution of findings: basilar predominance supports idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, whereas upper/mid-zone predominance or diffuse involvement suggests alternative diagnoses.
Correlate the specific combination of low lung volumes and basilar reticular opacities with restrictive physiology to confirm fibrotic etiology over cystic or air-trapping diseases.
